Element.attribute:
The Definition of Ready is a list of conditions that an item of work must meet to be considered eligible for a sprint. If these conditions are not met, the work cannot be considered for inclusion in a sprint.

Work items (i.e. Backlog Items) that are "ready" are clear, testable and feasible. An item of work is clear if the team has a shared understanding of the meaning, purpose and expected outcome. Clear definitions of work are written collaboratively and consistently alongside work items that are already considered "ready". A work item is considered testable if there is a clearly defined and effective way to determine if the outcome meets the expectations, even if the test itself does not exist yet. Finally, a work item is feasible if it can be completed within a single sprint, according to the Definition of Done. Work items that are too large to be considered feasible need to be broken down further so that they can be completed in a single sprint.

The main difference between the Definition of Ready and the Definition of Done is that the former provides guidance on when a work item is understood well enough, and the latter on when it can be considered complete.

Example criteria for a Definition of Ready include:

  • Acceptance criteria are well defined and testable
  • Business value is clearly articulated
  • Dependencies are identified and clearly stated
  • Work item has been estimated and is small enough to be completed in one sprint
  • Stakeholders are identified
  • Team understands how to demo the results of their work; including what should be presented to stakeholders to demonstrate that the expected outcome has been achieved

1. The Definition of Ready is not a static list. As the team and stakeholders learn more about the product already created and the creation process itself, they may update the criteria. It is important that revisions to the Definition of Ready are implemented prior to the start of a sprint as the pace of work would be disturbed if introduced during an in-flight sprint.
  2. It is recommended that dependencies between work items are avoided as it decreases the team's flexibility in deciding the order in which an item will be worked on during the sprint. Such lack of flexibility could lead to a mini-waterfall process. Team members can agree on shared results expected or create "mock/skeleton" elements to unblock development of a dependent work items.
  3. Each team must have a Definition of Ready appropriate for the work items they aim to complete. However, it is common practice for a number of teams developing elements of the same product to have shared or similar Definition(s) of Ready.
  4. Teams may use a list of criteria called INVEST as their first Definition of Ready, as it describes the minimum requirements for a well-written item of work.
To prevent the team from working on insufficiently refined requirements.

• List displayed in the team's working area, clearly visible to everyone
  • An electronically shared list such as one maintained in an electronic team collaboration tool, slide or spreadsheet
